newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM Hasina pleads unity, consensus.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM Hasina pleads unity, consensus.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, accused by opponents of trying to impose one-party rule, renewed her call on Wednesday for consensus on major national issues to ensure social and economic development.

"We are trying to establish an accountable and transparent government," Hasina told a conference of the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD), a party which lent support to her Awami League to form a government after June's general election.
"We want to forge a national consensus...to extend the fruits of independence to everyone," she said.
She called for "rock-like unity" among all parties to preserve independence, strengthen the economy, redress injustices and step boldly into the 21st century.
JSD chief A.S.M. Abdur Rob, whom Hasina appointed her shipping minister, reiterated his party's backing for Hasina's steps to end poverty and ensure equality in the eyes of the law.

The only other minister in Hasina's cabinet from outside her party is Communication Minister Anwar Hossain, secretary-general of the Jatiya party, headed by jailed former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad.
Hasina's arch rival, former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, accused her on Tuesday of conspiring to rehabilitate Ershad.

"A conspiracy is now on to rehabilitate a fallen autocrat. Such a move will jeopardise the country's hard-earned democracy," Khaleda, chief of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), said in a statement published on Wednesday.
"I urge all freedom and democracy-loving people to resist the conspiracy," she said.
Hasina on Wednesday also asked people to remain alert against what she called conspiracies to scuttle her efforts to put democracy on a solid foundation in the country.
Hasina and Khaleda together led a popular revolt in 1990 which toppled Ershad, a former army chief, nearly nine years after he seized power in a bloodless coup.
But they became rivals after Khaleda won a 1991 election and became Bangladesh's first woman prime minister.
Ershad, in jail since he lost power, contested the last election from jail as Jatiya chief and won five parliamentary seats.
